claim: In the United States, data centres account for nearly half of electricity-demand growth to 2030, and by the end of the decade the country is expected to use more electricity for data centres than for all energy-intensive goods production combined.
shortLabel: Data centres drive nearly half of U.S. demand growth
displayValue: Nearly half of U.S. demand growth through 2030
comparisonContext: This is the cleanest current way to explain why the U.S. grid story is more severe than the global one.
scopeNote: Share of growth, not share of total U.S. electricity demand.
